key_insight: A small six-site RNA splicing signature can reliably identify ReNU syndrome caused by RNU4-2 variants, especially T-loop variants.
clinical_relevance: This biomarker could support therapeutic development and future monitoring of treatment response in ReNU syndrome, with stronger signal in more severe T-loop cases.
method: Analyzed RNA-seq from two independent cohorts: 30 ReNU syndrome individuals and 54 controls.
Compared alternative splicing patterns and focused on shared alternative 5' splice-site events.
Derived a minimal six-site signature and tested it in blood controls and an iPSC-to-neuron model.
evidence_signal: The six-site signature perfectly separated 19 n.64_65insT cases from 54 controls and produced no false positives in 5,984 additional whole-blood controls.
watch_item: The biomarker appears specific to certain RNU4-2 variant classes, so broader validation is needed before it can be generalized across all ReNU syndrome patients.
paper_title: A cross-tissue splicing signature as a quantitative biomarker for ReNU syndrome
